..
Issued at 418 AM EDT Fri Oct 16 2026

Pattern Synopsis: Large scale pattern undergoing amplification 
across North America; long wave trough developing across eastern 
North America in response to upstream amplification across the 
Pacific basin with a +2 sigma 500mb height anomaly across western 
Canada/"peaking" +PNA teleconnection.  Consolidating short wave 
trough digging across the Midwest...phase lag between height/thermal 
troughs suggest continued deepening as the system swings through the 
Great Lakes/Ohio Valley later today.  Primary PV anomaly early this 
morning lies across Minnesota/eastern Nebraska with a secondary wave 
along back edge of deformation axis over far northwest Ontario. Deep 
layer moisture axis extends northeast from Texas into the Great 
Lakes...1.25-1.75 inch precipitable water values across Lower 
Michigan though drier air (in an absolute sense) is not far upstream 
on the backside of the approaching short wave trough.  In the wake 
of the upstream system...sub-zero 850mb temperatures spilling into 
the northern Plains within a 40-50kt northerly low level jet.  0400Z 
surface analysis shows a 1004mb low moving into southwest Lower... 
cold front trails to the southwest into southeast Illinois/southeast 
Missouri...warm front extends east into the Thumb.  Though the low 
itself is remarkably strong...a tight pressure gradient exists 
between the surface low and a 1044mb high over Montana/Wyoming 
(which is strong for mid October/+3 sigma MSLP anomaly and a roughly 
30 year return period).     

Primary Forecast Concerns:  

Windy today with continued rain chances: The Gales of October will 
arrive later this morning...with surface low tracking east-northeast 
across southern Lower Michigan this morning toward a 5mb/3h pressure 
fall center over Georgian Bay. Pressure gradient will tighten up 
across the forecast area in its wake...and low level cold advection 
will allow for a surface-based mixed layer to develop along with 
isentropic downsloping assisting in downward momentum transfer. 
Anticipating north/northwest wind gusts of 25 to 35 mph by late 
morning and continuing into early evening before winds slacken. 
Strongest wind gusts today expected along shoreline areas exposed to 
onshore flow...Gale Warnings are already up for all nearshore zones 
save for the St. Mary's River.  Rain remains widespread across Upper 
Michigan and the Tip of the Mitt counties early this morning...and 
has become more drizzly across the remainder of northern Lower.  As 
stronger dynamics sweep across Michigan later this morning with 
short wave trough arrival...expect additional shower activity likely 
aided by increasing instability over the surrounding Great Lakes. At 
this point doesn't look like any convective enhancement would be 
deep enough to support charge separation/thunder.  Precipitation 
coverage is expected to wane as the afternoon wears on...though some 
north flow lake induced showers may continue into the evening 
downwind of Lake Michigan/Lake Huron.  

Windy again Sunday but turning warmer: Tightening pressure gradient 
between high pressure stretching from New England across the Ohio 
Valley...and low pressure near Hudson Bay...will result in 
increasing southwest boundary layer flow into Michigan Sunday. Wind 
gusts again in the 25 to 35+mph range appear likely at this point. 
After a couple days of cooler temperatures today and Saturday (and 
likely some sub-freezing low temperatures Saturday morning)...we 
will return to the recent theme of October warmth. Sunday's breezy 
but sunny weather will be accompanied by temperatures warming back 
into the 60s (4 to 8 degrees above normal).    

Warming trend continues into next week: A Pacific-dominant flow 
pattern next week is expected to keep temperatures on the mild side 
by mid October standards...with highs likely approaching 70 degrees 
across parts of northern Lower Monday and Tuesday and Wednesday. 
Small chances for rain arrive for Thursday which could put a crimp 
in potential high temperatures...but at this point not looking for a 
return to near or below normal temperatures through Friday.
